haiku-low.q1: They see the generic message "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is stored or sent.
haiku-low.q2: The request is refused. The user sees the same generic message, with no reset row created and no email sent.
haiku-low.q3: A link works for 30 minutes. It ends sooner if it is used for a reset or if a newer link is issued, which marks older unused links as used.
haiku-low.q4: The link stays live and is not burned. The user can retry the form until the link expires.
haiku-low.q5: No devices stay logged in, since all sessions are deleted, including the current one. The user logs in again at the login page with the new password.
haiku-low.q6: The worker retries the send 3 times with backoff, then logs the failure and drops the job. The user is not told.
haiku-low.q7: The raw token is carried in the queued "reset" job, which the worker uses to build the emailed link. Only the hash is stored in the database.
haiku-low.q8: It hashes the token with SHA-256 and finds the password_resets row with that token_hash. It checks used_at is unset and expires_at is in the future.
haiku-low.q9: In the password_resets table, counted by user_id and created_at within the last hour. Requests age out of the rolling one-hour window as time passes.
haiku-low.q10: In the same transaction that inserts the new link, older unused rows get used_at set to now, which kills them.
haiku-low.q11: The password hash update, link claim (used_at) and sessions deletion happen in one transaction. The confirmation email is queued after COMMIT.
haiku-low.q12: The conditional UPDATE only succeeds when used_at is NULL and expires_at is in the future. The second submission updates zero rows and sees the expired page.

sonnet.q1: They see the generic message 200 "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is stored or sent.
sonnet.q2: Count of resets in the rolling hour is already >= 3, so the transaction is rolled back: no new row, no link, no mail. The user still sees the generic message.
sonnet.q3: Valid 30 minutes. Sooner: it is used (used_at set, by a successful reset), or killed (marked used) when a newer link is requested for the same account.
sonnet.q4: Still valid (not burned). The form is re-shown with an error and they can retry until it expires.
sonnet.q5: None: all sessions for the user are deleted, including the current device. The 302 goes to /login and no session is created, so they log in again with the new password.
sonnet.q6: The worker retries 3 times with backoff, then logs and drops the job. The user is not told; they get the generic message and can only request again (up to 3 per hour).
sonnet.q7: The raw token is put in the "reset" job enqueued on the email queue (user and raw token link), after COMMIT. The worker sends it through the mail provider. The job is removed after sending or failing, and payloads are never logged.
sonnet.q8: It computes sha256(T) of the token in the URL and finds the password_resets row with that token_hash. Invalid if no row, used_at is set, or expires_at < now(); otherwise valid and the form is shown.
sonnet.q9: It is not stored as a counter. It is computed by counting password_resets rows for the user with created_at > now()-1h, including killed and used rows. Old rows drop out as their created_at passes one hour; the optional cleanup deletes only rows more than 1 hour past expiry.
sonnet.q10: Earlier unused links are marked used (UPDATE used_at=now() WHERE user_id AND used_at IS NULL), in the same transaction as inserting the new row, before COMMIT and after the rate-limit check passes. So at most one live link.
sonnet.q11: In one transaction: the link is claimed (used_at set), the users password_hash is updated, and all the user's sessions are deleted. The "your password was changed" email is enqueued after COMMIT.
sonnet.q12: The conditional UPDATE (SET used_at=now() WHERE id=? AND used_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now()) inside the transaction. Only one updates a row; the other gets 0 rows updated, so it rolls back and sees the expired page.
